idiom_name: rpcgen-generated stubs over ONC RPC/XDR, or protobuf-c codecs over a hand-written socket framing
implementation_notes: C has no remote-interface concept, so the remote facade is assembled from a procedure table plus marshal/unmarshal functions: rpcgen compiles an interface written in the RPC Language into exactly that structure - *_clnt.c client stubs, *_svc.c server skeleton, *_xdr.c serialisation and a dispatch table that acts as the facade. Where the peers are not all C, protobuf-c generates only the message accessors (protoc-gen-c emits .pb-c.h/.pb-c.c; its former RPC layer now lives in the separate protobuf-c-rpc project) and the developer writes the framing, correlation and dispatch by hand. The classic rpcgen form is still justified when an existing ONC RPC/rpcbind estate or a freestanding target without a C++ or Rust runtime must be served.
pitfalls: rpcgen stubs return a pointer to a static result buffer, so concurrent requests in one server overwrite each other's reply; generate multithread-safe stubs or copy the result before returning.

XDR and protobuf-c payload ownership is manual: an unpacked message owns heap buffers that must be released (protobuf_c_message_free_unpacked), and mixing them with stack copies leaks or double-frees.
ONC RPC defaults to weak AUTH_UNIX credentials and a rpcbind/portmapper entry; a facade reachable from an untrusted network needs stronger authentication or must sit behind a firewall.
Hand-written socket framing without an explicit length prefix turns partial reads into silently truncated calls.
